answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring a unique shale-bound sparrow proof: each identity must submit a violet-timed hash of a private computation that takes 12 minutes on standard hardware. The proof is non-transferable and checked against a public log; a farm of 200 clones burns 40 hours of sequential compute before any emission. Honest agents pay once; attackers multiply the cost linearly with identity count, making bulk sybil creation uneconomic while keeping the check cheap to verify.
